title: Rolling-slate demand allocator: data-driven staff allocation & scope-cut matrix
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and roll out a ‘Rolling Slate Demand Allocator’ process: a data-driven decision framework and lightweight tooling that recommends how to apportion engineering and PM capacity across interdependent initiatives within a two-cycle rolling window. The allocator combines demand signals, skill match, priority elasticity, and risk to produce staff-band allocations plus a minimal scope-cut matrix that can be used in planning meetings and real-time rebalances.
background: We frequently face mid-cycle contention when high-priority incidents or enterprise opportunities surface. Current approaches (manual reassignments, ad-hoc freezes, or blunt scope cuts) cause churn and unclear accountability. The allocator aims to reduce frantic mid-cycle reshuffles by providing an auditable, repeatable recommendation that balances business priority, expected throughput, and specialist constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator produces per-initiative recommended FTE bands (min/target/max) for the upcoming 8-week window
Simulation runner shows expected delta in committed vs. delivered story points for 3 historical cycles within +/- 10% against actuals
Decision artifact includes a ranked scope-cut matrix (loss-minimizing) and a communication template for stakeholders
Piloted with two cross-functional initiatives (Console UX and Dedicated autoscaling) in Cycle 2026-W12 with no more than one emergency reassign per pilot week
Stakeholders (Eng leads, PMs, Design lead) sign off on the rubric and the first two-week reallocation run
plan: Week 1: Data discovery - collect historical velocity, skill rosters, on-call burn, and hotfix incidence by team
Week 2: Define demand signals and weights (customer impact, OKR alignment, revenue risk, latency SLO breach probability)
Week 3: Implement prototype allocator in a notebook and run simulations on last 6 cycles
Week 4: Convert prototype to lightweight spreadsheet + rules engine for review with Eng/PM leads
Week 5: Pilot run for two initiatives; gather feedback and iterate rubric
Week 6: Embed output into planning cadence and deliver communication/playbook
